goals.showColorBalanceDesc: Colors food items by calorie density per gram. Recommended for weight loss and appetite control.
goals.showColorBalanceInfoBody: Colors food items by energy density — i.e. how many calories the food contains per gram. Especially useful for weight loss and appetite control.
goals.showColorBalanceWhatBody1: The indicator shows how calorie-dense a food is. Foods with low energy density contain fewer calories per gram and often provide greater volume and better satiety for fewer calories.
goals.showColorBalanceWhatBody2: This can make it easier to stay full while staying within your daily calorie goal.
goals.showColorBalanceWhenBody1: The indicator is primarily designed for weight loss and appetite control.
goals.showColorBalanceWhenBody2: If your goal is muscle gain or weight gain instead, foods with higher energy density may be beneficial, as they make it easier to consume enough calories. In those cases the indicator becomes less relevant and can sometimes give a misleading signal.

weightTracker.title: Weight tracking
weightTracker.bodyFatNote: Does not affect your profile value.
weightTracker.noHistoryHint: Add your first weight measurement to start tracking
weightTracker.infoBodyFat: Body fat % measures what proportion of your total weight is fat. The value is recorded directly at each entry and gives a picture of your body composition over time.
weightTracker.infoBodyFatMass: Body Fat Mass is the actual weight of the fat in your body (kg), calculated as total body weight × body fat %. Unlike the percentage, this metric accounts for your total weight — an important perspective when analysing body composition.
weightTracker.infoSoftLeanMass: Soft Lean Mass is everything in your body except fat: muscles, bones, organs, blood and water. Calculated as total body weight minus Body Fat Mass. Often used as a measure of muscle building and the quality of weight loss.

macroDistribution.title: Macro distribution
macroDistribution.tooLow: Recommended: Adjust the ranges so the average approaches 100%.

macroDistribution.tip: The default values follow the NNR 2023 recommendations (Fat: 25–40%, Carbohydrates: 45–60%, Protein: 10–20%). You can adjust these freely between 0–100% for each macronutrient.

macroModes.ref_weightloss:
The protein range 1.2–1.6 g/kg comes directly from Leidy et al. (2015); Wycherley's meta-analysis supports that elevated protein during an energy deficit preserves fat-free mass (the high-protein arm averaged 1.25 ± 0.17 g/kg). Leidy also recommends ~25–30 g of protein per meal.

Deficit 20–25%: Wycherley's included trials used ~500–1000 kcal/day (most commonly 500 kcal ≈ 2092 kJ), in line with the classic 500–750 kcal/day guideline. For a typical user (TDEE 2000–2500), 20–25% equals ~450–625 kcal, squarely in that range.

The fat range 20–30 E% mirrors Wycherley's low-fat design (prescribed ≤30%, achieved 22–33%).

Leidy HJ, Clifton PM, Astrup A, et al. The role of protein in weight loss and maintenance. Am J Clin Nutr. 2015;101(6):1320S–1329S. doi: 10.3945/ajcn.114.084038. PMID: 25926512.

Wycherley TP, Moran LJ, Clifton PM, Noakes M, Brinkworth GD. Effects of energy-restricted high-protein, low-fat compared with standard-protein, low-fat diets: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. Am J Clin Nutr. 2012;96(6):1281–1298. doi: 10.3945/ajcn.112.044321. PMID: 23097268.
macroModes.ref_active:
The protein range 1.6–2.0 g/kg combines Morton's meta-regression — breakpoint 1.62 g/kg/day (95% CI 1.03–2.20), beyond which no further muscle gain was observed — with the ISSN recommendation of 1.4–2.0 g/kg for building and maintaining muscle. ISSN also recommends ~0.25 g/kg (20–40 g) of protein per dose, every 3–4 hours.

The fat range (20–35 E%) follows the Acceptable Macronutrient Distribution Range (AMDR) and is not specified in the protein studies.

Morton RW, Murphy KT, McKellar SR, et al. A systematic review, meta-analysis and meta-regression of the effect of protein supplementation on resistance training-induced gains in muscle mass and strength in healthy adults. Br J Sports Med. 2018;52(6):376–384. doi: 10.1136/bjsports-2017-097608. PMID: 28698222.

Jäger R, Kerksick CM, Campbell BI, et al. International Society of Sports Nutrition Position Stand: protein and exercise. J Int Soc Sports Nutr. 2017;14:20. doi: 10.1186/s12970-017-0177-8. PMID: 28642676.
macroModes.ref_nnr:
The macro distribution comes directly from the Nordic Nutrition Recommendations: fat 25–40 E%, carbohydrates 45–60 E%, and protein 10–20 E% — the ranges for healthy adults. The energy level is set at maintenance (TDEE ±3%) for weight stability.

The NNR is the scientific basis for the official dietary guidelines across the Nordic countries, produced by hundreds of researchers on behalf of the Nordic Council of Ministers.

Blomhoff R, Andersen R, Arnesen EK, et al. Nordic Nutrition Recommendations 2023. Copenhagen: Nordic Council of Ministers; 2023. Nord 2023:003. doi: 10.6027/nord2023-003.
macroModes.ref_offseason:
All values come directly from Iraki et al. (2019), Table 1: energy surplus +10–20% above maintenance, protein 1.6–2.2 g/kg, fat 0.5–1.5 g/kg, and remaining calories from carbohydrates (≥3–5 g/kg), targeting ~0.25–0.5% of bodyweight gained per week. Advanced lifters are advised to stay in the lower end of the surplus (+5–10%) to limit fat gain.

Iraki J, Fitschen P, Espinar S, Helms E. Nutrition Recommendations for Bodybuilders in the Off-Season: A Narrative Review. Sports (Basel). 2019 Jun 26;7(7):154. doi: 10.3390/sports7070154. PMID: 31247944; PMCID: PMC6680710.
macroModes.ref_onseason:
All values come directly from Helms et al. (2014), Table 1: protein 2.3–3.1 g/kg of fat-free mass (FFM), fat 15–30 E%, and remaining calories from carbohydrates, with a weight loss rate of ~0.5–1% of bodyweight per week (roughly a 20–25% deficit) to maximize muscle retention. The leaner you get, the higher within the protein range you should aim.

Helms ER, Aragon AA, Fitschen PJ. Evidence-based recommendations for natural bodybuilding contest preparation: nutrition and supplementation. J Int Soc Sports Nutr. 2014 May 12;11:20. doi: 10.1186/1550-2783-11-20. PMID: 24864135; PMCID: PMC4033492.
